rows.statement: A listed unit that fails to start, or cannot be added to the transaction, leaves the transaction valid and the configuring unit still starts.
rows.quote: this has no impact on the validity of the transaction as a whole, and this unit will still be started.

rows.statement: With or without After=, the configuring unit is stopped or restarted when a listed unit is explicitly stopped or restarted.
rows.quote: Besides, with or without specifying After=, this unit will be stopped (or restarted) if one of the other units is explicitly stopped (or restarted).

rows.statement: A listed unit that is not already started is not started by Requisite=, and the configuring unit's start fails immediately.
rows.quote: if the units listed here are not started already, they will not be started and the starting of this unit will fail immediately.

rows.statement: Beyond Requires=, BindsTo= also stops the configuring unit when a listed unit stops unexpectedly, which includes failure.
rows.quote: it also does so when a listed unit stops unexpectedly (which includes when it fails).

rows.statement: When systemd stops or restarts the units listed here, the action is propagated to this unit.
rows.quote: When systemd stops or restarts the units listed here, the action is propagated to this unit.

rows.statement: While the configuring unit is up, listed units found inactive or failed are started when no job is queued for them.
rows.quote: as long as this unit is up, all units listed in Upholds= are started whenever found to be inactive or failed,

rows.statement: Adds Requires= and After= dependencies for every mount unit needed to access the specified paths.
rows.quote: Automatically adds dependencies of type Requires= and After= for all mount units required to access the specified path.

rows.statement: The manual names including a unit in both After= and Wants= as a common pattern.
rows.quote: It is a common pattern to include a unit name in both the After= and Wants= options,
